frame.z: -elevM / 1000 (km below sea level, down positive); stations at sensorElevM

picks.fromUnusedStations: drop: picks from stations with usedInRun false (counts.picksFromUnusedStationsDropped)
picks.weights: none: PyOcto 0.2.0 has no per-pick weight; prob is only the threshold

postprocess.mergeRule: pairwise against a primary taken in rank order (most picks, earlier, lower index): origin times within mergeWithinS and shared picks >= fraction of the smaller event's picks; not transitive; absorbed picks keep the absorbed event's PyOcto residual
postprocess.minimumsReapplied: nPicks, nPPicks, nSPicks, nPAndSPicks and minStations before and after the shared-pick rule; an event dropped there returns its picks to the other events holding them and the rule reruns until no event is dropped
postprocess.pyoctoDeduplication: PyOcto deletes the smaller of two events sharing more than max_pick_overlap picks before this merge (no time condition, not counted here)
postprocess.sharedPickRule: a pick in two events stays with the smaller |PyOcto residual| (ties: more picks, earlier, lower index)

provenance.note: the code and software this stage ran with; ProcessingRun.gitSha and softwareVersions describe the run's creation

stations.aboveModelSourceTopNote: sensor elevation minus the velocity model's own top, for sensors above it: their tables run through the top layer extended upward over this thickness, so their predicted times are late where the ground there is faster; PyOcto station terms are 0 (statics come after location, LOC-05)
stations.stationTermsS: none: PyOcto adds 0 s for every station (statics come after location)

sweep.note: associated = events after this stage's post-processing at that point, before location; sweep.parquet (SweepPoint with located candidates, recoveredPublic and tierA) is written by LOC-06

tables.directoryRelativeTo: cache_dir (data/cache), or a temporary directory when associate() runs without cache_dir
tables.rowsAboveModelTop: repeat the top layer's velocities (PyOcto's n_padding is shared by all stations); no queried travel time passes through them

velocityModel.boundaryConvention: layer i spans topElevM[i+1] < elevM <= topElevM[i]: a point exactly on a boundary takes the layer below; the deepest layer is a half-space; above the top of the model is an error
velocityModel.conversion: topElevM = -TVDSS, in m above mean sea level with up positive. vpMPerS and vsMPerS are the source vp and vs unchanged (the source is already in m/s, so no unit conversion was needed). No value was edited, smoothed or resampled.
velocityModel.datum: topElevM is the top of each layer in metres above mean sea level (up positive), converted as elevM = -TVDSS, with mean sea level taken as NAVD88 orthometric height (the vertical of USGS 3DEP and run.yaml); the TVDSS datum (mean sea level, positive down) is established by the GDR 1613 methods report (p. 4 text ties the TVDSS column to mean sea level; p. 5 Fig. 3a shows it positive down with these layer tops), not by the velocity CSV, which only labels the column; the deepest layer is a half-space.
velocityModel.layerConvention: each source row is the top of one layer carrying that layer's constant Vp and Vs; the deepest row is the top of a half-space. The CSV does not state this; Fig. 3a of the same submission (methods report p. 5) shows it: its interfaces (green lines, digitized at TVDSS about -1598, -1230, -1030, -447, -316, 215 and 610 m) match rows 2-8, and the step velocities above the first interface (Vp about 2280 m/s, Vs about 1160 m/s) and below the last (Vp about 5520 m/s, Vs about 3330 m/s) match rows 1 (Vp 2296, Vs 1163 m/s) and 8 (Vp 5521, Vs 3334 m/s), which reading the rows as layer bottoms would contradict. The report (p. 4, Results) also describes eight layers about 130-580 m thick with Vp/Vs ratios of about 1.63-2.2. Row 1 (TVDSS -1800 m) is the model's formal top, not a resolved interface: Fig. 3a starts at about 1700 m ASL, near the local ground (1692.7 m ASL over the event-cloud centroid, USGS 3DEP 1 m via EPQS).
velocityModel.license: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), as stated on the GDR 1613 submission page
velocityModel.name: forge_1d_gdr1613_ver1
velocityModel.notes: Inverted jointly with the locations of 5 events (methods report p. 2, "Joint event location and velocity model inversion"; also Vera Rodriguez et al., SGW 2025, section 2.2, in GDR 1739) from DAS picks in wells 16B(78)-32 and 78B-32; the 257 events in the GDR 1613 DAS catalog lie at TVDSS 576-871 m (elevM -576 to -871). Rays therefore sample only the paths between that event cloud and those two wells, from the local ground (about 1693 m ASL there, so the first layer is sampled over only about 100 m) down to about -870 m ASL. Elsewhere, and deeper, the layer values and the half-space are extrapolation. Two velocity inversions are as published: layer 5 (Vp 5272) over layer 6 (Vp 5113), and layer 7 (Vp 5615, Vs 3374) over the half-space (Vp 5521, Vs 3334); the half-space Vp is about 5% below the 5.8 km/s basement of the GDR 1800 3D model. The same team later relocated these events with a dipping-layer 3D model from 2024 data, after the 1D locations disagreed with surface-network locations (Vera Rodriguez et al., SGW 2025, in GDR 1739); that 3D model is not published as a file. The GDR 1613 README calls the submission a preliminary data archive and its curator note anticipates updated VerX velocity-model files; none was published as of retrieval (2026-09-25: the submission lists only Inverted_1D_VelocityModel.csv, and GDR 1739 adds no velocity file).

source.citation: Vera Rodriguez, I., Wolpert, J., Podrasky, D., Coleman, T., Maldaner, C., Ma, Y., Chamarczuk, M., Becker, M., & Ajo-Franklin, J. (2024). Utah FORGE 3-2417: DAS Microseismic Event Catalog from the 16A/16B Circulation Test, 2023 [Data set]. Geothermal Data Repository, Rice University. https://doi.org/10.15121/2376139

velocityModel.sourceDatum: TVDSS is true vertical depth below mean sea level, positive down, so negative values lie above sea level. The velocity CSV only labels the column "TVDSS (m)"; the methods report of the same submission (FOGMORE_MEQ_Circulation2023.pdf) establishes the datum. Evidence: (1) p. 5, Fig. 3a plots this model's P and S step velocities and layer interfaces on an axis labelled only "TVDSS (km)" that runs from about -1.70 km at the top to about +0.90 km at the bottom, which shows the sign (positive down) but does not name the datum; (2) p. 4 (Results) gives the located microseismicity a "depth range of 570 m to 750 m from mean sea level", which matches the "TVDSS (m)" column of the same submission's event catalog (FORGE_DAS_event_catalogue_circulation.csv, 5th-95th percentile 584-746 m, n = 257) and so ties that column to mean sea level; (3) the same team's final relocated catalog (GDR 1739, Header_Description.txt) defines its depth column as hypocentral depth from mean sea level.

topExtension.note: Vp and Vs above fromElevM are the source's top layer extended upward; the source has no values there

velocityModel.verifiedBasis: verified: true means the values, the TVDSS datum and the layer-top reading all come from the GDR 1613 submission itself (the velocity CSV, and the methods report's p. 4 text and p. 5 Fig. 3a). The NAVD88 reading of mean sea level and any top-layer extension are ours; they are stated in datum and topExtension.

volume.note: bbox projected to ENU plus volume.horizontalMarginM, from topElevM (null: run.refSurfaceElevM, not the local ground) down to bottomElevM; it is not the locator's volume. Association elevM is preliminary: it may lie above the local ground and must not be shown without relocation

window.rule: events with origin time outside [startS, endS) are dropped after the duplicate merge (counts.droppedOutsideWindow); the bbox is not applied here

locate.arrivals: one row per event x used station x phase; tPred = origin time + table travel time + static; tObs/residualS/pickId null without a pick; usedInLocation false for outlier-dropped picks and rows without a pick
locate.eventId: hq-<runId>-<6 digits>, numbered from 0 in origin-time order (ties: assocId)
locate.flagsTable: locate_flags.parquet (H2-internal): eventId, assocId, mapOnVolumeTop, mapOnVolumeBottom, depthOnEdgeTop, depthOnEdgeBottom, topFaceMass, bottomFaceMass, pdfTruncated, nodeBudgetHit, hErrGridLimited, vErrGridLimited, nDroppedPicks, outlierPassSkipped, nearestStationSurfaceElevM, aboveNearestStationSurface
locate.meanPickProb: mean prob of the picks in pickIds (picker confidence)
locate.pickIds: picks used in the final location (outlier-dropped picks left out)

statics.note: additive per (stationId, phase); the statics table holds the map every event without its own used (hq.locate.statics)

locator.misfit: sum_i w_i |t_obs_i - T_i - static_i - t0|, w_i = prob_i / sigma_i; t0 = lower weighted median of (t_obs_i - T_i - static_i) (eliminated analytically)
locator.outliers: drop |residual| > max(madK * MAD, floorS), MAD unscaled over both phases; relocate once

provenance.note: the code and software this stage ran with; ProcessingRun.gitSha and softwareVersions describe the run's creation

locator.search: coarse grid over the volume; a fineStageSpacingM pass from the first fine box (fineHalfWidthM around the best coarse node) grown until the region within pdfCutoff clears every non-volume face; fine nodes over that region, grown the same way; both stop at maxPdfNodes (then hErrM/vErrM are None, pdfTruncated); hypocentre = fine MAP node

velocityModel.layerConvention: each source row is the top of one layer carrying that layer's constant Vp and Vs; the deepest row is the top of a half-space. The CSV does not state this; Fig. 3a of the same submission (methods report p. 5) shows it: its interfaces (green lines, digitized at TVDSS about -1598, -1230, -1030, -447, -316, 215 and 610 m) match rows 2-8, and the step velocities above the first interface (Vp about 2280 m/s, Vs about 1160 m/s) and below the last (Vp about 5520 m/s, Vs about 3330 m/s) match rows 1 (Vp 2296, Vs 1163 m/s) and 8 (Vp 5521, Vs 3334 m/s), which reading the rows as layer bottoms would contradict. The report (p. 4, Results) also describes eight layers about 130-580 m thick with Vp/Vs ratios of about 1.63-2.2. Row 1 (TVDSS -1800 m) is the model's formal top, not a resolved interface: Fig. 3a starts at about 1700 m ASL, near the local ground (1692.7 m ASL over the event-cloud centroid, USGS 3DEP 1 m via EPQS).
velocityModel.license: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), as stated on the GDR 1613 submission page
velocityModel.name: forge_1d_gdr1613_ver1
velocityModel.notes: Inverted jointly with the locations of 5 events (methods report p. 2, "Joint event location and velocity model inversion"; also Vera Rodriguez et al., SGW 2025, section 2.2, in GDR 1739) from DAS picks in wells 16B(78)-32 and 78B-32; the 257 events in the GDR 1613 DAS catalog lie at TVDSS 576-871 m (elevM -576 to -871). Rays therefore sample only the paths between that event cloud and those two wells, from the local ground (about 1693 m ASL there, so the first layer is sampled over only about 100 m) down to about -870 m ASL. Elsewhere, and deeper, the layer values and the half-space are extrapolation. Two velocity inversions are as published: layer 5 (Vp 5272) over layer 6 (Vp 5113), and layer 7 (Vp 5615, Vs 3374) over the half-space (Vp 5521, Vs 3334); the half-space Vp is about 5% below the 5.8 km/s basement of the GDR 1800 3D model. The same team later relocated these events with a dipping-layer 3D model from 2024 data, after the 1D locations disagreed with surface-network locations (Vera Rodriguez et al., SGW 2025, in GDR 1739); that 3D model is not published as a file. The GDR 1613 README calls the submission a preliminary data archive and its curator note anticipates updated VerX velocity-model files; none was published as of retrieval (2026-09-25: the submission lists only Inverted_1D_VelocityModel.csv, and GDR 1739 adds no velocity file).

Utah FORGE 3-2417: DAS Microseismic Event Catalog from the 16A/16B Circulation Test, 2023 [Data set]. Geothermal Data Repository, Rice University. https://doi.org/10.15121/2376139

velocityModel.sourceDatum: TVDSS is true vertical depth below mean sea level, positive down, so negative values lie above sea level. The velocity CSV only labels the column "TVDSS (m)"; the methods report of the same submission (FOGMORE_MEQ_Circulation2023.pdf) establishes the datum. Evidence: (1) p. 5, Fig. 3a plots this model's P and S step velocities and layer interfaces on an axis labelled only "TVDSS (km)" that runs from about -1.70 km at the top to about +0.90 km at the bottom, which shows the sign (positive down) but does not name the datum; (2) p. 4 (Results) gives the located microseismicity a "depth range of 570 m to 750 m from mean sea level", which matches the "TVDSS (m)" column of the same submission's event catalog (FORGE_DAS_event_catalogue_circulation.csv, 5th-95th percentile 584-746 m, n = 257) and so ties that column to mean sea level; (3) the same team's final relocated catalog (GDR 1739, Header_Description.txt) defines its depth column as hypocentral depth from mean sea level.

topExtension.note: Vp and Vs above fromElevM are the source's top layer extended upward; the source has no values there

velocityModel.verifiedBasis: verified: true means the values, the TVDSS datum and the layer-top reading all come from the GDR 1613 submission itself (the velocity CSV, and the methods report's p. 4 text and p. 5 Fig. 3a). The NAVD88 reading of mean sea level and any top-layer extension are ours; they are stated in datum and topExtension.

uncertainty.calibration: coverage of the 68% errors is measured, not assumed: the synthetic test records it (fracHWithinHErrM, fracVWithinVErrM) for the geometry it ran on
uncertainty.depthOnEdge: > 0.05 of the mass on the evaluated fine grid's top face or on its bottom face (docs/02)
uncertainty.gridFloor: lambda_max and the vertical variance are floored at spacing^2 / 12 (flagged)
uncertainty.hErrM: sqrt(chi2_2(errConfidence) * lambda_max): semi-major axis of the horizontal marginal's confidence ellipse, lambda_max the largest eigenvalue of the 2x2 horizontal covariance
uncertainty.mapOnVolumeFace: separate from depthOnEdge: EventLocation.map_on_volume_top / map_on_volume_bottom and search['mapOnVolumeTop'] / search['mapOnVolumeBottom'] are true when the MAP node lies within mapOnVolumeFaceBandM of the search volume's top / bottom (a PDF pinned there by the volume prior; its formal errors are cut off by it)
uncertainty.pdf: node mass proportional to exp(-pdfMisfitScale * misfit); pdfMisfitScale 1 is the Laplace likelihood with scale sigma/prob per pick, profiled over the origin time (weighted median), uniform prior over the fine nodes; normalised to sum to 1 over the evaluated fine nodes. Formal errors only: the hypocentre is the least-misfit node
uncertainty.truncation: the evaluated region grows until no face other than the volume's top or bottom holds a node within pdfCutoff of the minimum; if a lateral volume face or maxPdfNodes stops it, hErrM and vErrM are None and the search record says pdfTruncated
uncertainty.vErrM: standard deviation of the vertical marginal (68% in 1D)

uu.description: km below sea level. UUSS Catalog Details, "Format for Earthquake Summary Data", Depth column: the depth datum is sea level for earthquakes from Oct 1, 2012 on (1.5 km above sea level before that in the Utah region). ComCat: the depth datum depends on the contributing network. ComCat serves QuakeML 1.2, which defines Origin.depth relative to nominal sea level (WGS84 geoid); UUSS's own statement above agrees.
uu.label: km below sea level (UUSS catalog depth datum)

provenance.note: the code and software this stage ran with; ProcessingRun.gitSha and softwareVersions describe the run's creation

magnitude.status: none: stage tier rewrote events.parquet with every magnitude null; stage magnitude (MAG-01) fills them, writes magnitude.json and replaces this record

arrivalWindows.rule: [t + R / vMax + static - pad, t + straight-ray time + static + pad] per phase (static: the station-phase's statics.parquet term, 0 without one), clipped to the run window

chanceTimeCoincidences.rule: nLocated * 2 * maxDtS / window length: located origin times uniform over the run window; the distance limit is ignored

match.cost: |dt| / dtScaleS + epicentral distance / distScaleM (magnitude not used)
match.distance: horizontal ENU (EPSG:32612 minus run origin); grid scale factor negligible
match.lowestCost: in unmatched reasons, the located event (or associated candidate) with the lowest cost; it can be far from the public event in time or space
match.objective: most admissible one-to-one pairs, then least total cost (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment)

provenance.note: the code and software this stage ran with; ProcessingRun.gitSha and softwareVersions describe the run's creation

match.sensitivityRule: each pair reruns the assignment as both limit and cost scale

calibration.note: bars are the calibration run's ProcessingRun.tiering thresholds (its matched set), applied unchanged; none derived from this window

tiering.caveat: Public regional catalog events are the larger ones, so bars drawn from the recovered public events are conservative for small candidate events.
tiering.claim: Strict (Tier A): on each metric separately, at least as good as a bar that at least 75% of the recovered public regional catalog events with a value on that metric meet or beat.
tiering.definition: Per metric and tier, the bar is an actual matched event's value: sort the events of the matched set M with a value on the metric from best to worst and take the ceil((1 - q) * n)-th, n = their count, q = tiering.quantiles[tier]; at least (1 - q) of them meets or beats the bar (boundary equality passes). A (Strict): every A bar, depthOnEdge false, mapOnVolumeTop false when locate flags are given, and quality.minEpiDistM <= strictNearestStationFactor * focal depth. B (Good): every B bar. C (Candidate): associated and located, outside those ranges.
tiering.eventPicks: one Pick per id in each final event's pickIds (picks used in the final location); eventId set, residualS from arrivals.parquet
tiering.final: SeismicEvent rows as this stage writes them: located columns unchanged, tier, tierReasons, catalogMatch from matches.parquet, magnitude null (stage magnitude, MAG-01, fills it afterwards), revealOrder -1

matchedSet.definition: located candidate events with a public regional catalog match (matches eventId not null)
matchedSet.meetingEveryBarNote: matched events meeting every metric bar of the tier at once (the A rules are not applied here; counts.matched has the matched events' tiers)

tiering.matchesChecked: every matched row's dtS / distM equals what events_located and catalog give now (a match from before stage locate's statics pass 2 is refused)

provenance.note: the code and software this stage ran with; ProcessingRun.gitSha and softwareVersions describe the run's creation

mapOnVolumeTop.note: from locate_flags.parquet (MAP within locator.mapOnVolumeFaceBandM of the search-volume top)

nearestStation.focalDepth: sensorElevM - elevM of the epicentrally nearest station with a pick used in the final location (arrivals.usedInLocation, stations.parquet): the event's depth below that station's sensor, a borehole's depth included; an event at or above the sensor fails the rule
nearestStation.test: quality.minEpiDistM <= factor * focal depth (epicentral distance to the nearest station with a pick used in the final location)

rules.nullErrors: a null hErrM or vErrM fails A and B on that metric; bars on those metrics are drawn from the matched events with a value (nUsed of n; nNull recorded), so a null never loosens a bar

thresholds.method: rank ceil((1 - q) * n) from the best: numpy inverted_cdf at 1 - q for lower-is-better metrics; for higher-is-better ones its mirror -inverted_cdf(-v, 1 - q), the largest value at least (1 - q) of M meet or beat (one rank above inverted_cdf at q when q * n is an integer)

velocityModel.boundaryConvention: layer i spans topElevM[i+1] < elevM <= topElevM[i]: a point exactly on a boundary takes the layer below; the deepest layer is a half-space; above the top of the model is an error
velocityModel.conversion: topElevM = -TVDSS, in m above mean sea level with up positive. vpMPerS and vsMPerS are the source vp and vs unchanged (the source is already in m/s, so no unit conversion was needed). No value was edited, smoothed or resampled.
